caveats:
This map was derived from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images acquired by the ALOS-2 satellites operated by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) before (17 Mar 2020) and during (27 Sep 2022) the event.

These are preliminary maps derived from satellite radar and should be used as guidance only. Coloured pixels may include false positives, and their absence does not mean an absence of damage or flooding.
methodology_other: Change detection on synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite images acquired before and after the event. Damage Proxy Maps show significant changes in radar coherence and amplitude; Flood Proxy Maps show areas that changed to standing water. Maps are preliminary and checked against news reports and ground-level imagery where available.

# EOS-RS Flood Proxy Map: Philippines, Typhoon Noru, 27 Sep 2022, v0.5

The Earth Observatory of Singapore - Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS) created this preliminary Flood Proxy Map (FPM) depicting areas that are likely flooded in Luzon, Philippines due to Typhoon Noru (Karding) which made landfall on 25 Sep 2022. This map was derived from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images acquired by the ALOS-2 satellites operated by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) before (17 Mar 2020) and during (27 Sep 2022) the event.

The image covers an area indicated by the large white polygon. Each light blue pixel measures about 25 meters across. Preliminary validation was done in selected areas using optical imagery. This flood proxy map should be used as a guide to identify areas that are likely flooded, and is less reliable over urban and vegetated areas.

Data were provided by Sentinel Asia and analyzed by the Earth Observatory of Singapore - Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS).

**More map details and files:** <https://sf.earthobservatory.sg/event/EOS-RS_202209_Philippines_Typhoon_Noru>

**More map details and files:** <http://eos-rs-products.earthobservatory.sg/EOS-RS_202209_Philippines_Typhoon_Noru/>

organization.description: The Earth Observatory of Singapore - Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS) is a research lab at Nanyang Technological University (NTU), Singapore. It uses satellite remote sensing, mainly synthetic aperture radar (SAR), to map natural hazards and disasters. The lab produces Damage Proxy Maps (DPMs) and Flood Proxy Maps (FPMs) showing where damage or flooding has likely occurred. Its work focuses on Southeast Asia and the wider Asia-Pacific, and it also responds to major disasters worldwide.
